Subject: Strategy for hosted → dedicated migration + sizing data request

Connor — thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited to finalize the commitment and target Dedicated for Q4. Before we lock terms, your engineering team asked for traffic and latency samples to validate GPU sizing and cutover windows. I attached a CSV with 30 days of peak and p95 token rates (zettacorp_current_traffic.csv).

High-level asks from my side:
- Can Redwood confirm a conservative GPU count and an alternate burst pool configuration for our enterprise SLA (50ms median target)?
- How long should we schedule for a production cutover (canary → full cutover) assuming a staged migration by region?
- Any immediate blockers from our procurement side? Procurement has requested a mutual action plan and an initial roll schedule we can share with legal.

I'm looping procurement on the thread. Appreciate a short runbook-style response we can use internally.

Best,

ZettaCorp

Elena — thanks for the CSV, that was really helpful. I did a quick pass with our sizing tool and sketched a conservative starting point. High level answer first, then action items below.

Summary (conservative):
- Baseline GPUs for steady-state: 6 x A100-80GB (or equivalent) for your current p95 token profile.
- Burst / canary pool: 2 x smaller nodes (e.g., A10 or 1/4-quant instances) to absorb traffic spikes during rollout and for fast fallback.
- Expected end-to-end cutover (canary → 100%): 2–3 weeks calendar, with one week of canary + staged regional ramp-ups. Total black-box testing + regression: ~4 business days.

Immediate action items:
1) Karthik to run an inference bench with the attached CSV and send the detailed GPU matrix.
2) Marissa to prepare a draft mutual action plan and proposed contract amendment for your procurement team.
3) I'll set up a canary runbook + rollback checklist and propose concrete dates.

I've attached a placeholder matrix (proposed-gpu-matrix.xlsx) — Karthik will replace it with validated numbers by tomorrow. If that timeline works, can we target an initial canary the week of 2026-08-24?

Connor O'Brien
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference

On Mon, Jul 20, 2026 at 4:14 PM Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Elena — thanks for the CSV...

Elena & team — I ran the traffic trace through our perf harness using the model artifact you plan to serve (l4-large-open) and a standard quantized path. Results below are conservative (we include a 20% safety multiplier for p95 SLA headroom):

- Observed p95 tokens/sec: 9,200 (from CSV peaks)
- Single A100-80GB effective throughput at p95 (with batching=auto): ~1,450 tokens/sec
- Required baseline GPUs = ceil((9,200 * 1.2) / 1,450) = 8 GPUs (A100-80GB-equivalent)
- Recommended production config: 6 dedicated GPUs + 2 hot-standby in the same tenancy (makes rollbacks and burst easier).
- Canary sizing: run canary on 1 GPU + 1 burst node (A10). Test with 10% of traffic for 72 hours, verify latency & error budgets, then 25% for 72 hours, then 100%.

Notes:
- If you accept a slightly higher p95 target (70ms), baseline drops to 5 GPUs. Let us know trade-offs.
- We're assuming persistent KV cache warmup is allowed during the canary. If caching is cold on cutover, allow an extra 24 hours for ramp.

Proposed timeline (detailed):
- Day 0–2 (pre-cut): infra prep, pipeline validation, IAM & network checks (Redwood + Zetta networking).
- Day 3–9 (canary weeks): 10% traffic → 25% traffic → 50% (week-by-week checkpoints).
- Day 10–14: full cutover and switch traffic routing, post-cut regression window.

I'll push an updated proposed-gpu-matrix.xlsx with the math and instance recommendations to the Drive link.

—Karthik
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: mutual_action_plan_v3.docx (we will finalize after procurement feedback)
